chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Isma'il told me, saying: Al-Bajiri narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Harb al-Wasiti narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Harun, from Abi Shayba, saying: A man from Hamedan narrated to us, from his father, saying: Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said:

The five pioneers are: I am the pioneer of the Arabs, Salman is the pioneer of the Persians, Suhayb is the pioneer of the Romans, Bilal is the pioneer of the Ethiopians, and Khabbab is the pioneer of the Nabataeans.
ai.seo_question: Who are the five pioneers mentioned by Ali ibn Abi Talib in al-Khisal?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) designates Salman al-Farsi, Suhayb al-Rumi, Bilal al-Habashi, and Khubayb al-Nabati as the 'pioneers' (sabbāq) for their respective ethnic groups, establishing a model of universal Islamic leadership that transcends tribalism. This classification underscores the Shia emphasis on the meritocratic nature of the early community, where spiritual precedence is determined by faith and service rather than lineage, reflecting the Quranic principle that nobility lies in piety alone.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-90 Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Isma’il narrated that Al-Bajiri quoted Muhammad ibn Harb al-Vaseti, on the authority of Yazid ibn Harun, on the authority of Abi Shoyba’, on the authority of a man from Hamedan, on the authority of his father that Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB) said, “

There are five pioneers. I am the pioneer of the Arabs. Salman Farsi is the pioneer of the Persians. Saheeb is the pioneer of the Romans. Bilal is the pioneer of the Ethiopians. And Khibab is the pioneer of the Nabataeans .”
